text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- Newspaper says that delays in restructuring the Romanian Oil Company threaten its future.
- The newspaper quotes Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu as saying that the government will not intervene in the market to determine grain prices.
ADEVARUL
- The European Commission left Romania out of a list f the first six countries expected to start EU membership talks next year.
- The government has failed so far to start real restructuring of loss-making energy-consuming industries, the newspaper says in an editorial.
- Parliament postponed adopting a key land bill on Tuesday when senators of the ruling coalition showed up in insufficient number to ensure passage.

- Romania's rail authority SNCFR will get loans worth a total $217 million from the World Bank and the EBRD for track repairs and maintenance. The Romanian government is also due to put $163 million in the project to upgrade rolling stock.
- Lack of state-allocated funds means more than two million tonnes of wheat from Romania's 1997 bumper crop estimated at 7.07 million tonnes will not find buyers.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Romania cannot afford to become a member of the European Union in its current economic situation, Integration Minister Alexandru Herlea said in an interview. He said Romania's economy was weak and needed strong reforms.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- More than one third of Romanian families live in dire poverty, the newspaper quotes a survey by the Institute for Study of the Quality of Life.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- President Emil Constantinescu met Emperor Akihito during a five-day visit to Japan.
ADEVARUL
- More than 23,000 people have already been laid off from the education system as a result of restructuring measures under a 1997 austerity budget.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea says the Peasant Party will meet Democratic Party leaders throughout August to patch up recent rifts between the ruling coalition partners.
- The leftist opposition Party of Social Democracy held a protest rally outside the education ministry over changes to the education law adopted by government decree. ($ = 7,135 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
